title: DOCK2, trauma and PTSD: DNA methylation and gene expression
purpose: Universal Mind is investigating whether its interventions, developed around hypotheses concerning oxytocin receptor signalling, are associated with changes in DOCK2 gene expression or DNA methylation. DOCK2 is an exploratory biological outcome alongside symptoms, functioning and wellbeing. The aim is to test whether it can provide an early signal of intervention response.

DOCK2 means dedicator of cytokinesis 2. It is distinct from the DOC2 family. Published human studies connect DOCK2 with PTSD-associated methylation, with limited expression evidence and mixed replication. These observations motivate a longitudinal research question; they do not establish a beneficial direction of change or a validated surrogate for recovery.

Research purpose: intervention response, not initial diagnosis. The proposed chain from an intervention to OXTR-related biology, to DOCK2 change, to clinical benefit contains several untested links. Measuring each link separately keeps the hypothesis testable. Literature reviewed 21 November 2026; this is a targeted narrative evidence map, not a systematic review.
reviewMethod: Targeted narrative evidence map. Supplied links screened; primary results and relevant full-text passages assessed where accessible. Not a systematic review or clinical biomarker validation.
duplicateSuppliedLink: The Frontiers 2022 review appears twice in the supplied PDF; one source is retained.

records.title: Genomewide DNA methylation analysis in combat veterans reveals a novel locus for PTSD
records.design: Human blood methylation and expression; 96 veterans and 115 independent replication participants
records.summary: Lower methylation at DOCK2 cg16277944 was associated with greater PTSD symptom severity and replicated in a separate cohort (p = 0.0028). Post-hoc blood analyses found a modest inverse methylation–expression association (r = −0.21) and a group difference in DOCK2 expression.
records.limitation: Cross-sectional, male samples; discovery used a 10% false-discovery-rate threshold. Association does not establish intervention responsiveness. Genetic variation also influenced methylation. The 211 participants are the total across both cohorts, not the discovery sample alone.
